description: Committee approved $630,600 in social service cash grants.
Funds will support 29 Saskatoon community agencies.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Kelleher praised non-profits as more efficient and effective than the municipality.
CLASSIC and Foundations Learning advocated for continued city investment in non-profits.
CLASSIC assists Indigenous women, refugees

speakers.name: Chantelle Johnson
speakers.organization: Community Legal Assistance for Saskatoon and Area
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: CLASSIC - 2026 Community Cash Grants
said: Non-profits fill service gaps and reduce strain on public systems.
Social grants provide stability, expand programming, and prevent higher costs.
Investing in legal clinics like CLASS saves $6-10 for every dollar.

speakers.name: Sheryl Harrow-Yurach
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Foundations Learning and Skills Sask - 2026 Community Cash Grants
said: Foundations Learning builds practical skills for adults and families.
City grants ensure free programs and match volunteers with adults.
City investment is infrastructure for a caring community.

description: Committee recommends $1.2 million in 2026 tax abatements.
Funds 31 eligible recreation, social services, and culture groups.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
5 for, 0 against
Abatements for 6 recreation, 18 social services, and 7 culture organizations.
Delegates from Broadway Theatre and Craft Council supported abatements
Program supports Indigenous creators and provides accessible cultural opportunities.

speakers.name: Lenore Maier
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: The Broadway Theatre - 2026 Community Tax Abatements
said: Tax abatement allows reinvestment into programming, accessibility, staffing, and community outreach.
Generates economic benefits by attracting 75,000 visitors, supporting local businesses.
Provides stable funding, crucial for operations, especially with flat provincial arts funding.

speakers.name: Jeff Erbach
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Sask Craft Council - 2026 Community Tax Abatements
said: Abatement allows directing resources to public programs and business development, not building maintenance.
Council acts as a steward of a heritage building, providing cultural access and programming.
Aligns with city's strategic plan, supporting economic development and Indigenous creators.

description: Adds 'Hawthorn' and 'Sunrise' to city's master name list.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Councillor Parker praised the engagement process, stating it was money well spent.
The naming process involved targeted community engagement, an exception to existing policy.
Elders and youth advocated for 'Sunrise' due to its traditional and ceremonial significance.
The naming process prioritized Indigenous community engagement for inclusive names.
Administration will present revised naming policy updates within several months.

speakers.name: Nora Cummings
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: University Heights 3 Neighbourhood
said: Elders and youth chose "Sunrise" for its traditional meaning.
Hopes council honors indigenous people's decision for the name.
Indigenous people should have a say in naming land.
